title: Build a byte-pair tokeniser and measure what it charges
brief: Turn text into bytes, train a byte-pair encoder and replay it to encode and decode, then measure fertility, tokens per character, and digit cuts.
hints: text_to_bytes is list(text.encode('utf-8')). An accented letter gives two numbers and an emoji gives four, so the list can be longer than the string.
unknown_rate splits the text with text.split(), counts the words that are not in word_vocab, and divides by the number of words. Return 0.0 when there are no words.
get_pair_counts walks each inner list on its own: for a, b in zip(tokens, tokens[1:]): counts[(a, b)] = counts.get((a, b), 0) + 1. A word with the pair twice adds 2.
merge_pair scans with a while loop. On a match write new_id and move on by two, otherwise write the current id and move on by one. That is why [5, 5, 5] becomes [20, 5].

train_bpe splits with _pretokenize, turns each piece into a list of bytes, and loops while 256 + len(merges) < vocab_size. Pick the winner with min(counts, key=lambda p: (-counts[p], p)), store vocab[256 + i] = vocab[a] + vocab[b], then merge. Stop when get_pair_counts returns an empty dict.
apply_merges_to_word starts from ids = list(word_bytes). For each i, pair in enumerate(merges), call merge_pair([ids], pair, 256 + i) and keep the first list it returns.
encode loops over _pretokenize(text), turns each piece into list(piece.encode('utf-8')), replays the merges on it, and extends one flat list.
decode is b''.join(vocab[i] for i in ids).decode('utf-8'). Decoding one id at a time breaks on a character split across two tokens.
fertility is len(encode(text, merges)) / len(text.split()). Split on whitespace, not with _pretokenize.
tokens_per_char divides by len(text), which counts characters. With no merges a three-byte character costs 3.0.
digit_token_lengths encodes the text, looks up vocab[i] for every id with build_vocab(merges), counts the bytes in range 48 to 57, and keeps counts above 0.
